Subject: Quick question on buying path & co-sell incentives

Hi Laura / Marcus,

We're close to finalizing our internal approval for the pilot but procurement raised a couple of routing questions that I wanted to clarify before we lock dates:

1) If we purchase via AWS Marketplace (private offer), will the invoice show up on our AWS bill and still qualify for Redwood's co-sell program?
2) Alternatively, if we do a direct Redwood contract (PO + invoice), how does co-sell compensation / partner credits work on your side?

We're trying to decide which path shortens procurement while preserving any reseller/co-sell discounts the AWS team might offer. We also need to confirm whether any SOC2 or audit artifacts need to be attached to the order.

We have a soft go/no-go on Sept 15 — would appreciate a short rundown so we can advise procurement. Attached our internal checklist and a sample sandbox quote for numbers.

Hi Samantha — great questions. High-level answer up front: both paths are supported, but they differ on billing, timing, and how co-sell incentives are handled. See brief comparison below and a recommended mutual action plan at the end.

Marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP private offers):
- Invoice appears on your cloud provider bill (consolidated) which many customers prefer for easier cost allocation.
- Marketplace private offers can be processed faster for procurement teams that already buy through the provider.
- Co-sell: Redwood participates in cloud co-sell programs. To qualify we need the listing tied to an eligible partner account and a co-sell nomination (we coordinate with the partner team). Some cloud incentives require a marketplace purchase; others require partner paperwork — we can confirm specifics with the cloud rep.

Direct contract (Redwood PO / Invoice):
- Invoice comes from Redwood (you receive vendor invoice). This is usually straightforward for customers who require vendor invoices or need custom legal terms not supported in a marketplace private offer.
- Co-sell: We can still enable partner/co-sell compensation, but it typically requires an internal nomination and an attribution workflow (takes a bit longer). For large deals we often set up a short partner referral addendum to capture incentives.

Other considerations:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2 summary, audit logs) — we can attach a SOC2 summary and SOC2 controls workbook to the procurement packet for either path.
- Billing reconciliation: marketplace reduces vendor management overhead but sometimes complicates custom tax/PO flows.
- Entitlements & BOM: If you plan to use Dedicated or Private deployments, we may need a slightly different ordering flow (work with AE to lock down SKUs).

Recommended next steps (mutual action plan):
- Today: I can confirm the exact co-sell eligibility with our cloud partnerships team (quick check).
- Mon: Marcus to produce two one-page order options (Marketplace private offer vs Redwood direct) with invoice examples and estimated timing.
- Wed: We send a short packet (Doc with SOC2 excerpt + quote + marketplace private offer link) to your procurement.

I'll loop in Vanessa (our channel & marketplace lead) for the co-sell specifics and attribution steps.

Best,
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: Quick question on buying path & co-sell incentives

Adding the channel perspective — short answers to the two procurement points: 

1) Marketplace invoice + co-sell: Yes, Marketplace purchases can qualify for co-sell, but we need two things before incentives flow: (a) a co-sell nomination in the partner portal tied to the customer account, and (b) the offer recorded with the same Seller ID that we use for partner attribution. If procurement buys a private offer, ask them to keep the PO reference (we use that to match back).

2) Direct invoice + co-sell: We can do partner attribution retroactively but it requires the partner rep to submit the opportunity and revenue details. That typically adds ~1–2 weeks to incentive processing. For your timeline, marketplace private offer + immediate co-sell nomination is likely the fastest way to ensure both procurement speed and incentive eligibility.

Note on Azure / GCP: the high-level mechanics are similar, but the exact partner portal and timeline vary. If you prefer Azure or GCP, we'll confirm portal steps in parallel.

I'll prepare a one-pager outlining the nomination checklist and a sample private offer link you can share with procurement.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Channel & Marketplace Lead, Redwood Inference

Jordan — quick confirmations inline:
- Marketplace private offer: you should still supply a PO number when requesting the private offer; include the PO in the private offer request so it shows up on the provider invoice. That meets most finance teams' PO controls.
- Direct invoice: we can accept an invoice-to that differs from the legal entity, but we need a short billing addendum capturing remit details. Marcus will add the billing addendum template to the packet.

Attached: a short packet with (1) marketplace private offer checklist and example PO flow, (2) Redwood direct invoice + billing addendum template, (3) SOC2 summary. Marcus — can you upload the two quote variants to HubSpot and trigger the DocuSign envelope (DEAL-9851)?

Samantha / Jordan — I'll follow up with the actual marketplace private offer link as soon as it's provisioned. If you want to move quickly, sign the direct quote and we can do retroactive partner nomination for co-sell attribution (Vanessa noted that may add ~1–2 weeks on incentives processing).
